l1: Knows why the same property, entity or party appears under different names and IDs
l2: Matches records to master entities and maintains identifier crosswalks
l3: Designs entity hierarchies and matching rules; resolves conflicts between sources; reviews others' matches
l4: Owns a master-data approach used across clients

name: Pipeline monitoring and data observability
description: Monitoring pipelines and data health (DataOps): freshness, volume, schema changes, alerts and data contracts with providers.
l1: Knows the signs of a failed or stale feed (freshness, volume, schema)
l2: Monitors feeds and loads; acts on alerts and failed jobs
l3: Sets monitoring and alert thresholds; agrees data contracts with providers; cuts the time to detect and fix
l4: Their observability standards are adopted across the platform

name: Scripting and workflow automation
description: Automating routine work with scripts and workflow tools: Python, SQL, spreadsheet automation and low-code.
l1: Knows which repeated tasks can be automated
l2: Writes scripts that automate parts of profiling, mapping or checking
l3: Builds tested, version-controlled automation that others on the team run
l4: Their automation and its standards are adopted across the service line
source: L1-L4: chan-cxmds.md (B8.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: AI-assisted data processing
description: Using AI to classify, extract and suggest mappings in data processing, with human review of every output.
l1: Knows where models help with data work (classification, extraction, mapping suggestions) and how they fail
l2: Uses AI tools to suggest mappings or classify fields, and reviews every output before use
l3: Builds AI-assisted steps with confidence routing, human approval, logged decisions and measured accuracy
l4: Contributes to the organisation's policy on where model judgement is allowed in data work; other teams adopt their method, or they publish it
